hero.intro: I produce, mix and master music — and write score and sound design for screen. Twelve years of Hindustani vocal training and western classical guitar sit behind every decision I make at the desk.

about.portraitAlt: Abhishek Venkatasubramanian singing into a microphone during a live performance
about.lead: I am an audio engineer who produces, mixes and masters tracks — and a musician first.
paragraphs: I trained in Indian classical music (Hindustani vocal) for over a decade and in western classical guitar alongside it. That double training is the reason I hear arrangement problems before I hear mix problems: if the parts are fighting for the same space, no amount of EQ will rescue them.

I hold a Bachelors of Audio from SAE Institute Dubai, and I have worked across live sound, studio assisting, media production and music education. My own catalogue runs from Hindi and Tamil originals to devotional bhajans and instrumental fusion, plus covers — and on the screen side, score and sound design for trailers, commercials and game media.

I work the same way on every project, whether it is a single voice and a guitar or a full arrangement: get the source right, protect the emotion of the take, and make the record translate on the devices people actually listen on.
about.philosophy: Serve the song, not the session.

process.title: Talk first
process.body: A short call about the song, the reference tracks you love, and what you want a listener to feel. No brief, no start.

process.title: Get the source right
process.body: Most mix problems are recording problems. If we are tracking, we fix them at the microphone rather than at the plugin.

process.title: Build the balance
process.body: Arrangement before EQ. If two parts are fighting for the same range, one of them moves.

process.title: Reference and revise
process.body: You hear it against the tracks you chose, on the systems you actually use. Two rounds of revisions come as standard.

process.title: Deliver properly
process.body: Master, platform versions, stems and documentation — everything you need to release without coming back to ask.

faq.q: What do you need from me to start a mix?
faq.a: Stems exported from the top of the session at the same sample rate, with no master-bus processing, plus two or three reference tracks and any rough mix you have been living with.
Two rounds on mixing and production, one on mastering. Beyond that we agree a rate before any further work.
Yes. Most work is remote — files in, files back, with a call at the reference stage.

faq.q: Which languages do you work in?
faq.a: Hindi, Tamil and English. Classical vocal training means I can follow and direct a take in Hindustani idiom as well as pop phrasing.
Yes — trailers, commercials, games and film scenes, delivered as stems to your spec.

contact.note: Tell me about the song, when you need it, and send a reference track or two. I reply within two working days.
contact._privacyNote: The old Wix contact page also published a full home address and a date of birth. Both are deliberately left off this site: together they are the raw material for identity theft, and a residential address adds a personal-safety exposure that wins no work. Clients need a city and a way to reach you. Add them back only as a deliberate choice.

demoAudio.note: These are synthesised demonstration files shipped with the site so the player and the A/B comparison work out of the box. Replace them with real excerpts — see HANDOVER.md, 'Adding your own audio'.

player._note: The tracks in the player at the bottom of every page. While isDemo is true the site labels them as demonstration audio, because they are synthesised placeholders rather than real recordings. Replace src with your own excerpt (MP3, 30-60 seconds is ideal), set isDemo to false, and the label disappears.

compare._note: The before/after control. 'raw' should be a rough bounce and 'mixed' the finished version OF THE SAME PERFORMANCE. Both files are played at a matched loudness so a listener is comparing the mix and not the volume.
compare.title: The same take, two chains
compare.blurb: A mix is not a volume control. Switch between the rough bounce and the finished version — both play at the same loudness, so what you hear is the balance, the tone and the space, not one being turned up.
